newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent close down after NYMEX breaks key suppor.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent close down after NYMEX breaks key suppor.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures wiped all their early gains plummeting to a settle below the $18 psychological support level on Friday after NYMEX's WTI contract plunged to a 15 month low, traders said.

July Brent closed a hefty 62 cents a barrel down at $17.70, missing by three cents a nine-month low for the front-mont contract on April 4, when the May contract closed at $17.67. July Brent, however, briefly touched a low of $17.59 towards the close.
"The fall was all technically-led prompted by NYMEX's fall," one broker said.
"Towards the close there was good selling," he added.
NYMEX's July WTI contract closed 84 cents down at $18.82 after breaking through key support at $18.96, a double-bottom on the spot chart created April 10.
July Brent traded early in the day at the $18.48 level, some 80 cents above the close, and hit a high of $18.51 a barrel.

"We seemed to be very much following NYMEX...As soon as gasoline went through its support level every one was waiting for that," one trader said, as the London market began hitting the red in the late afternoon, pulled down first by fund selling on NYMEX heating oil then unleaded gasoline.
The WTI contract for July was hit hard by speculative and trade selling, traders said.
Earlier on Friday, IPE gas oil futures closed lower, pulled down by a falling NYMEX complex.
June gas oil, which had a hit a high of $168.25 a tonne, closed $1.50 down at $164.25 a tonne, while July gas oil ended the day $2.00 lower at $165.75 a tonne.
